Further - Suspected impressment of
Chinese by Japanese Authorities.

At 11 a.m. 1/3/41, the missing man's father
reported that his son had been released. The latter
was therefore brought to the station and under interro-
gation gave the following account of the incidents:-
    At 6 p.m. 27/2/41, he was crossing from North
to South over the Garden Bridge en route to his place
of employment, the Dah Tuh Iron Works located at Hart
and Kiaochow Roads corner. He had in his possession
several articles of wearing apparel and bedding
contained in a haversack of the style used in the
Japanese Army. He was stopped by the Naval Sentry at
the Bridge and then removed to the Naval Sub-Station
at Chapoo and Tiendong Roads corner. He was detained
there until 9 p.m. and it was here that he wrote the
messages referred to in the first report. At the hour
mentioned he was removed by truck to the Gendarmerie
Station at the North Railway Station where he was
questioned regarding the origin of the haversack. He
explained that he had found same in Kootung about four
years ago and the authorities concerned being satisfied
with his story released him at 9 a.m. 1/3/41.

另——怀疑日本当局强征中国人。

1941年3月1日上午11时，失踪者的父亲报告称其子已被释放。该男子随后被带到警局，经讯问后对事件经过作了如下陈述：
    1941年2月27日下午6时，他在前往位于哈同路（Hart Road）与胶州路（Kiaochow Road）转角处的达铁工厂（Dah Tuh Iron Works）上班途中，正由北向南穿过外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）。他随身携带一个日式军用背包，内装数件衣物和被褥。他在桥上遭到海军哨兵拦阻，随后被带至乍浦路（Chapoo Road）与天潼路（Tiendong Road）转角处的海军分驻所。他被拘押至晚上9时，并在此期间写下了第一份报告中提及的纸条。在上述时间，他被用卡车押送至北站宪兵队驻地，当局就背包的来源对他进行了盘问。他解释说该背包是大约四年前在虹口（Kootung）捡到的。有关当局对其说法表示满意，遂于1941年3月1日上午9时将其释放。

#1

1.

now
Hongkew
February 28th, 41.

Suspected impressment of Chinese
by Japanese Authorities.
------------------------------------

At 4 p.m. 28/2/41, one Wong Kyung Sung (黃京生):
Fireman fitter No.212, attached to Hongkew Fire Station
Workshops, reported at the station that his son had
been impressed by Japanese Military Authorities.

Under interrogation he stated that his son
left his home at Lane 36/7 Kashing Road for no
definite purpose at 6 p.m. 27/2/41 and up until now
had failed to return. At about 1 p.m. 28/2/41, an
unknown male Chinese of the coolie class called at the
Hongkew Fire Station and handed the missing man's
father his son's pocket book. Without asking for any
explanation as to how the stranger came by the pocket
book, the father left for home with the object of
getting a dollar to pay him for his service. On his
return, however, the stranger had left. The pocket
book contained eight pencilled chits (translations
attached) addressed to various relatives in which the
missing man stated that he had been impressed by
Japanese Military. The notes contained no information
as to the circumstances attending his impressment.
The writing is identified by the father as being that
of his son.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

涉嫌日本当局强征中国人。
---

1941年2月28日下午4时，黄京生（Wong Kyung Sung）：
系虹口消防站车间所属第212号消防员兼技工，至警局报案称其子被日本军事当局强征。

经讯问，他陈述其子于1941年2月27日下午6时离开嘉善路36弄7号住所，并无明确目的，至今未归。1941年2月28日下午1时许，一名身份不明的华籍苦力男子来到虹口消防站，将失踪者的钱包交予其父。该父亲未询问陌生人如何获得此钱包，便回家取一美元以酬谢其服务。然而当他返回时，陌生人已离去。钱包内装有八张铅笔书写的纸条（附译文），写给各位亲属，失踪者在其中陈述自己被日本军方强征。纸条中未包含有关其被强征经过的任何信息。其父辨认出字迹为其子所写。

page_data.en:
Translation

Please deliver the message to one Wong Kyung Sung,
Hongkew Fire Station.
I named Tsai Ling, was impressed by Japanese Army.
Please don't worry.

My wife Tsung Pao,
I would meet you again in the next world. Please don't
worry. Please take care of my little daughter.

Mr. Mother-in-law,
I would meet you again in the next world. Please don't
worry.

Gentlemen/Ladies,
Please deliver this message. There is $1.00 inside as
fare.

(Remaining five notes are repetitions of the above).
page_data.zh:
译文

请将此信转交虹口消防站的一位名叫 Wong Kyung Sung（音译）的人。
我名叫 Tsai Ling（音译），深受日军震撼。
请勿担忧。

吾妻宗宝（Tsung Pao，音译）：
我们来世再相见。请勿担忧。请照顾好我的小女儿。

岳母大人：
我们来世再相见。请勿担忧。

诸位先生/女士：
请代为转达此信。内附一元，作为邮资。

（其余五张便条内容同上）。

FORM 40
C. U 1-40

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Sung Chaung Soon (申長松)
native of Kompo taken by A/c D.I. Kao Yen Ken, J.D.C. 19.
at Sp.Br.Hqr. on the 25-2-41 translated
and transcribed by Clerk Tan Hsuen Hua

My name is Sung Chaung Soon (申長松), aged 49, a
native of Kompo, married coolie No. 1207, employed at the
Public Lavatory of the P.W.D., S.M.C. at the corner of Ping-
liang Road near Nwei Nan Road, and residing at a house (number
unknown) in the Lao Wen Teh Li (文德里), Yangtszepoo Rd.
off Tseu Ka Pai Road.

At about 4.50 a.m. on February 16, 1941, I left my home
to proceed to the An Tung Road Depot of the P.W.D. to report
for duty. While proceeding from East to West along Yangtszepoo
Road, at about 5 a.m., I observed a company of about 1,000
Japanese soldiers marching in formation from West to East along
Yangtszepoo Road. I was stopped and seized by one of their
number and instructed to carry a wooden box, which weighted
about 100 catties, together with another male Chinese who had
also been commandeered by the Japanese soldiers.

Whilst proceeding with the Japanese soldiers along
Yangtszepoo Road, near the Ta Kong (大康) Cotton Mill, I
noticed the Japanese soldiers seized a fish monger, who was
riding on a tricycle. The Japanese soldiers forced the fish
monger to ride the tricycle in front, whilst we (another male
Chinese and myself) were told to place the wooden box we were
carrying on the tricycle and to hold it there.

In the meantime, three other male Chinese were likewise
commandeered and told to perform the same kind of work.
Altogether about 200 male Chinese were commandeered.

At about 9 a.m. February 16, 1941, we arrived at the
Jukong Wharf, where we were told to take the wooden boxes on
board a Japanese steamer moored along side the wharf.

表格 40
C. U 1-40

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为申長松（Sung Chaung Soon）之供词，该员系江苏高邮（Kompo）人，由代理督察高仁肯（Kao Yen Ken）于1941年2月25日在特别分部总部讯问取得，并由书记员谭宣华（Tan Hsuen Hua）翻译及誊录。

本人名申長松，现年49岁，江苏高邮（Kompo）人，已婚，苦力编号1207，受雇于工部局工务处，在该处位于平凉路近威海路转角之公共厕所任职，现居住于曹家牌楼路杨树浦路文德里内某号房屋（门牌号不详）。

1941年2月16日凌晨约4时50分，本人离家前往工务处安东路堆栈报到上班。沿杨树浦路由东向西行进时，约在凌晨5时许，本人看见约一千名日本士兵列队沿杨树浦路由西向东行进。本人被其中一名士兵拦下并抓住，奉命与另一名同样被日本士兵征用的中国男子共同搬运一只木箱，该木箱重约一百斤。

当本人随日本士兵沿杨树浦路行进至大康纱厂附近时，注意到日本士兵抓获了一名骑三轮车的鱼贩。日本士兵强迫该鱼贩在前方骑行三轮车，同时命令我们（另一名中国男子和本人）将所搬运的木箱放置在三轮车上并扶住固定。

与此同时，另有三名中国男子也被征用，奉命从事同样的工作。总共约有二百名中国男子被征用。

1941年2月16日上午约9时，我们抵达掘孔码头（Jukong Wharf），奉命将木箱搬上停靠在码头旁的一艘日本轮船上。

FORM 40
G. P.M.-1.40

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of
native of ____ taken by me
at ____ on the ____ and interpreted by ____

- 2 -

After boarding the steamer, we were separated into several
groups guarded by a number of soldiers and the steamer later
sailed.

At about 3 p.m., each of us was given a cooked rice
ball to eat, without vegetable.

At about 10 a.m. on February 17, 1941, the steamer
arrived at the Tien Sung Kong Wharf where we were told to
unload the wooden boxes from the ship to the wharf.

Having disembarked from the ship, a Japanese soldier
spoke, in Shanghai dialect, and told us to fall in on the
wharf, whereupon a roll call was made. A cooked rice ball
was then given to each of us on the wharf.

At about 2 p.m. that day (February 17), we marched
from the Tien Sung Kong Wharf to a hospital in the walled city
of Nantung, arriving there at about 5 p.m.

At about 8 p.m. February 17, we were each again given
a cooked rice ball to eat.

At about 4 p.m. the following day, February 18, we
resumed our march and proceeded outside the walled city of
Nantung to a country place.

A Japanese officer, armed with a sword, arrived on
the scene and speaking in Shanghai dialect, asked if any of us
were commandeered from Shanghai. Twelve of us raised our hands
to indicate that we had come from Shanghai. A Japanese soldier
then instructed all twelve of us to return to the hospital in
Nantung.

About 5 a.m. the next day, February 19, 1941, we left

登上轮船后，我们被分成数个小组，由多名士兵看守，随后轮船启航。

下午3时许，每人分得一个熟米饭团食用，没有蔬菜。

1941年2月17日上午10时许，轮船抵达天盛公码头（Tien Sung Kong Wharf），我们奉命将船上的木箱卸至码头。

下船后，一名日本士兵用上海话讲话，命令我们在码头上列队，随即进行了点名。随后在码头上每人分得一个熟米饭团。

当日（2月17日）下午2时许，我们从天盛公码头出发，步行前往南通城墙内的医院，于下午5时许抵达。

1941年2月17日晚上8时许，我们每人再次分得一个熟米饭团食用。

次日，即2月18日下午4时许，我们继续行进，离开南通城墙，前往一处乡下地方。

一名佩带军刀的日本军官到达现场，用上海话询问我们中是否有人是从上海被征调来的。我们中有十二人举手示意来自上海。随后，一名日本士兵指令我们十二人全部返回南通的医院。

次日，即1941年2月19日凌晨5时许，我们离开

the hospital and proceeded to the Tien Sung Kong Wharf. It was still curfew hour on the wharf and a policeman appeared and took us to a Police Station in Tien Sung Kong, where another police officer told us to stay in a guild called Li Nyi Dong ( 礼 义 堂 ), in Tien Sung Kong, stating that a blockade was in force on the Yangtsze River and no shipping facilities were then available.

While staying in Tien Sung Kong, we were employed as coolies on the wharf and each day the police there distributed 12 "sen" (12/100 of a "zar") of rice for our food together with fuel for cooking the rice.

At 10.30 a.m. on February 22, 1941, a Japanese Gendarme gave me a steamer ticket and I boarded a Shanghai bound steamer on which I arrived at Pootung at about 10 p.m. 22/2/41. I took a ferry across the Whangpoo and arrived at the Canton Road bund the same night.

On February 24, 1941, I reported for duty at the Antung Road Depot as usual. At about 2 p.m. 24/2/41, I reported the above to the Yangtsepoo Police Station accompanied by a coolie-foreman named Hai Yung ( 海 榮 ) of the R.W.D.

All the male Chinese commandeered by the Japanese soldiers were not paid any wages.

The above is my true statement.

Sung Chaung Soon
(Signed and cross-marked)

医院，随后前往天盛公码头。当时码头仍处于宵禁时段，一名警察出现并将我们带至天盛公的一处警察局，另一名警官指示我们留在天盛公一个名为“礼义堂”的公所内，并称长江已实施封锁，目前无航运设施可用。

在天盛公停留期间，我们在码头充当苦力，当地警察每日分发 12 “仙”（即 1/100 “元”）的大米作为我们的口粮，并提供煮饭所需的燃料。

1941 年 2 月 22 日上午 10 时 30 分，一名日本宪兵给了我一张轮船票，我登上了一艘驶往上海的轮船，并于 1941 年 2 月 22 日晚上 10 时左右抵达浦东。当晚我乘渡轮横渡黄浦江，抵达广东路外滩。

1941 年 2 月 24 日，我照常到安顿路车栈报到上班。1941 年 2 月 24 日下午 2 时左右，我在杨树浦警察局报案陈述上述经过，陪同我前去的是一名来自水道处的苦力头目，名叫海荣 ( Hai Yung )。

所有被日本士兵征用的中国男性均未获得任何工资。

以上是我的真实陈述。

宋庄顺 ( Sung Chaung Soon )
（签名并画押）

FORM 49
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Chang Sung Kun (張昇坤),
native of Shanghai taken by D.I. Kao Yen Ken, C.D.C. 83.
at Sp.Br. Hqrs. on the February 25, 1941, translated Clerk Tan Hsueh Hua
and interpreted by

My name is Chang Sung Kun (張昇坤), aged 57, a
native of Shanghai, married coolie No.1243 employed at the
Antung Road Depot of the Public Works Department, S.M.C., and
residing at No.72, Yih Zung Li (依仁里), Yangtszepoo
Road.

At about 5.30 a.m. February 16, 1941, I left my home
to proceed to the Antung Road Depot. Whilst walking from
East to West along Yangtszepoo Road, near Sungpan Road, I
observed a company of about 200 Japanese soldiers marching in
formation from West to East along Yangtszepoo Road. One of
these soldiers suddenly stopped me on the way and seized hold
of me, whereupon an army wooden box, which weighted about
30 catties, was placed on my back and I was instructed to
follow them. Whilst marching along with the soldiers, more
than ten other Chinese were commandeered by them en route and
forced to carry boxes.

At about 8 a.m. we arrived at the Jukong Wharf where we
were relieved of the wooden boxes. The Japanese soldiers then
boarded a Japanese steamer taking with them their wooden boxes.
Some 10 soldiers were left behind and these escorted us on
board a motor boat. After I boarded the motor boat, I noticed
that there were about 200 other Chinese already commandeered on
the boat.

About half an hour later, the boat sailed. At about
5 p.m. same day, (February 16, 1941) we were given one cold
cooked rice ball each for a meal.

At about 9 a.m., February 17, 1941, the boat arrived

警务调查报告。
以下为张昇坤（Chang Sung Kun，上海籍）之陈述，由特别分部总部（Sp.Br. Hqrs.）刑事侦缉科第83号侦探督察高仁肯（D.I. Kao Yen Ken, C.D.C. 83）于1941年2月25日录取，由书记员谭学华（Tan Hsueh Hua）翻译并担任口译。

本人姓名张昇坤，现年57岁，上海籍，已婚，系工部局工务处安东路堆栈雇用的苦力，编号1243，居住于杨树浦路依仁里（Yih Zung Li）72号。

1941年2月16日上午5时30分许，本人离家前往安东路堆栈。当沿杨树浦路由东向西行走至松潘路附近时，本人看见约200名日本士兵成纵队沿杨树浦路由西向东行进。其中一名士兵突然在路上拦住本人并将本人抓住，随后将一个重约30斤的军用木箱放在本人背上，并命令本人跟随他们前行。在随士兵行进途中，又有十余名中国人在路上被其强征，被迫搬运木箱。

上午8时许，我们抵达菊功码头（Jukong Wharf），卸下了木箱。日本士兵携带木箱登上一艘日本轮船。约有10名士兵留下，护送我们登上一艘摩托艇。本人登上摩托艇后，注意到船上已有约200名其他被强征的中国人。

约半小时后，船只启航。同日（1941年2月16日）下午5时许，每人分发一个冷饭团作为餐食。

1941年2月17日上午9时许，船只抵达

The following is the statement of

at Tien Sung Kong (天生港) where we disembarked, after
which we were again given one cold cooked rice ball each .

Following our arrival at Tien Sung Kong, the Japanese
soldiers, about 200 in number, also disembarked and unloaded
their wooden boxes from the steamer. We were told to carry
these boxes for them and to march together with the 200 soldiers
and the other 10 soldiers who were acting as our escort. At
about 5 p.m. that day (February 17) we arrived at a place
inside the walled city of Nantung, which appeared to be a
hospital and in which we were lodged together with the soldiers.
Some 60 commandeered Chinese were placed in each room guarded
by a Japanese soldier. At about 9 a.m. we were given one hot
cooked rice ball each.

At about 10 a.m., the following morning, February 18,
1941, we were again given one hot cooked rice ball each.

At about 2 p.m., the same day, February 18, we were
told to carry a wooden box each and resume our march together
with the Japanese soldiers. After marching for about 20
Chinese "li", we arrived at the country side and were told to
unfasten the wooden boxes from our backs and to place them in
the field. A Japanese army officer, accompanied by a Chinese
interpreter, then arrived and asked if any of us were comman-
deered from Shanghai. He said that those who had come from
Shanghai should raise their hands, whereupon 12 of us did so.
The twelve of us were then told by the Officer to return to
Shanghai.

I asked the Japanese officer if we were to be given our

我们在天生港（Tien Sung Kong）下船，随后每人又分得一个冷的熟米饭团。

我们抵达天生港后，约二百名日本士兵也下了船，并从轮船上卸下他们的木箱。我们奉命为他们搬运这些木箱，并与这二百名士兵以及另外十名担任我们护卫的士兵一同行进。当天（2月17日）下午五时左右，我们到达南通城墙内的一处地点，该处看似一家医院，我们与士兵们一同被安置在此住宿。每个房间关押了约六十名被征用的中国人，由一名日本士兵看守。上午九时左右，每人分得一个热的熟米饭团。

次日，即1941年2月18日上午十时左右，我们每人再次分得一个热的熟米饭团。

同日，即2月18日下午二时左右，我们奉命每人背负一个木箱，随日本士兵继续行进。行进了约二十华里后，我们到达乡下，并奉命解开背上的木箱，将其放置在田地里。随后，一名日本军官带着一名中国翻译到来，询问我们中是否有人是从上海被征用来的。他说，从上海来的人应当举手，于是我们中有十二人举了手。随后，该军官命令我们这十二人返回上海。

我问日本军官，是否会把我们的

- 3 -

passage money. In reply he said that we would not be given
any passage money and that if we wished to receive any money,
we would have to continue working for them.

We then returned immediately to the hospital where
we stayed the night but we had nothing to eat.

At about 6 o'clock the following morning, February
19, all twelve of us proceeded to the Tien Sung Kong Wharf.
It was still curfew hour on the wharf and a Chinese policeman
arrived on the scene and questioned us. We told him of our
plight in detail. When he learned that we had not eaten since
10 a.m. the previous day (February 18), when each of us ate
a cooked ride ball, he immediately bought a number of Chinese
cakes and distributed two cakes to each of us.

At this point, two Japanese soldiers arrived on the
scene and the Policeman told them of our plight. The two
Japanese soldiers then took us to their headquarters.

At about 11 a.m., whilst we were in the Japanese army
headquarters, we were given 6 "sen" of rice (6/100 of a "zar")
and were told to cook the rice in the kitchen for our meal.

Whilst thus detained in the Japanese army headquarters,
we were employed in transporting flour for the Japanese. We
stayed there for four days during which period we were each
day given one "sen" of rice each without vegetables and told
to cook the rice for ourselves. During the night we slept on
the floor.

At about 5 p.m., February 22, 1941, a Chinese coolie-
foreman arrived and told us to leave for Shanghai. We asked

船费。他回答说，我们不会得到任何船费，如果我们想要拿到钱，就必须继续为他们工作。

随后我们立即返回医院，在那里过夜，但没有任何食物可吃。

次日（2月19日）早晨约6时，我们十二人一同前往天通庵码头（Tien Sung Kong Wharf）。当时码头仍处于宵禁时段，一名中国警察赶到现场并对我们进行询问。我们将自身的困境详细告知了他。当他得知我们自前一天（2月18日）上午10时起便未进食，当时每人仅吃了一个熟山芋球，他随即购买了一些中式糕点，分给我们每人两块。

此时，两名日本士兵到达现场，该警察向他们说明了我们的困境。随后，这两名日本士兵将我们带往他们的司令部。

上午约11时，我们在日本陆军司令部期间，获发了6“仙”的大米（即1“扎尔”的百分之六），并被告知在厨房将米煮好作为餐食。

在被拘禁于日本陆军司令部期间，我们受雇为日本人搬运面粉。我们在那里停留了四天，在此期间，每天每人仅获发1“仙”的大米，没有蔬菜，并被告知自行煮饭。夜间我们睡在地板上。

1941年2月22日下午约5时，一名中国苦力工头到来，吩咐我们动身前往上海。我们问道

The following is the statement of Pan Fung Di ( 潘 功 疊 )
native of Ningpo taken by me C.D.S. 30
at Po e Hdqrs. on the 25.2.41 and interpreted by Clerk Tan Hsueh Hua

My name is Pan Kung Di alias Lee Lou Ling
(李茂林). I am a native of Ningpo, aged 48, and
residing at No.217 Doong Woo Lee ( 同和里 ), at the
corner of Glen and Haichow Roads. I am employed at
the Antung Road Depot of the S.M.C. P.W.D. as
scavenger No.1200.
At out 5.15 a.m., February 16, 1941, when
I was passing the corner of Lincheng and Yangtszepoo
Roads on my way from home to the Antung Road Depot, I
saw some 1,000 Japanese soldiers proceeding from West
to East along Yangtszepoo Road on foot, and I also saw
that some 400 Chinese had been conscripted by the
Japanese soldiers. At the same time, a Japanese
soldier approached and seized me. He ordered me to
leave my dust sweeper and dust bin and assist another
Japanese soldier in carrying a wooden box. He stated
that it would take me only about 15 minutes. I
complied with the order and followed the party of
Japanese soldiers. The wooden box weighed about
60 catties, and I did not know the contents. On
Arrival at the Jukong Wharf, Civic Centre, Kiangwan,
at about 8 a.m., I requested the Japanese soldier, who
had conscripted me, to release me. Instead of
allowing me to leave, he took off my red jacket bearing
the No.1200, issued by the P.W.D., and threw it into
the Whangpoo River. At 10 a.m., I and other conscripted
coolies were each given a ball of cooked rice. When

以下为潘功叠（宁波籍）之陈述，由本人 C.D.S. 30 于 1941 年 2 月 25 日在捕房总部录取，并由职员谭学华翻译

我叫潘功叠，别名李茂林。我是宁波人，现年 48 岁，居住在格伦路（Glen Road）与海州路（Haichow Road）转角处的同和里 217 号。我在工部局工务处安通路堆栈担任第 1200 号清道夫。
1941 年 2 月 16 日上午 5 时 15 分左右，当我从家中前往安通路堆栈途中，经过临青路与杨树浦路转角处时，我看见约 1,000 名日本士兵沿杨树浦路由西向东步行前进，我还看见约 400 名中国人被日本士兵强征。当时，一名日本士兵走近并抓住了我。他命令我放下扫帚和垃圾箱，协助另一名日本士兵搬运一个木箱。他说这只需要占用我大约 15 分钟时间。我服从了命令，跟随那队日本士兵前行。木箱重约 60 斤，我不知道里面装的是什么。上午 8 时左右到达江湾市中心区虬江码头时，我请求那名强征我的日本士兵释放我。他非但没有让我离开，反而脱下了我身上印有第 1200 号码的工务处红色夹克，将其扔进了黄浦江。上午 10 时，我和其他被强征的苦力每人分到了一团熟米饭。当

we had eaten the rice ball, the Japanese soldiers
instructed us to carry wooden boxes, bread and other
things aboard a number of large and small naval ships
berthed alongside the Jukong Wharf. We were shut
up in the cargo holds of the ships. I was on one of
the naval ships in company with some 60 other coolies
we
guarded by 7 or 8 Japanese soldiers. The
ship sailed at 12 noon but could not make out in
what direction the ship was going.

At 8 a.m., February 17, the ship arrived at
Tien Sun Kong, Nantung, Kiangsu, where we were ordered
ashore. We were lined up on the wharf and I noticed
that there were altogether more than 1,000 conscripted
Chinese coolies. Immediately afterwards, we were
employed to carry ammunition and other military supplies
to a place within the Nantung walled city which is
about 30 or 40 li (about 10 miles) inland from the River.
During the night we were accommodated in a building which
looked like a hospital or school. There were 17 or 18
rooms in the building. More than 60 coolies stayed in
each room which was guarded by a Japanese soldier. At
3 p.m., February 18, we were told to leave the building
and proceed via the same route to the wharf.

When we were en route from the Nantung City
Wall to the wharf at Tien Sun Kong, Nantung, a Japanese
military officer asked us if we were natives of Shanghai.

我们吃完饭团后，日本士兵命令我们将木箱、面包及其他物品搬运至停靠在菊工码头（Jukong Wharf）的多艘大小军舰上。随后我们被关押在船舱内。我与大约60名其他苦力同在一艘军舰上，由7或8名日本士兵看守。该船于中午12时启航，但我无法辨认船只航行的方向。

2月17日上午8时，船只抵达江苏南通的天生港（Tien Sun Kong），我们奉命上岸。我们在码头上列队，我注意到被征用的中国苦力总数超过1000人。紧接着，我们被派往将弹药及其他军需物资运送至南通城墙内的一处地点，该地距离江边约三四十里（约合10英里）。夜间，我们被安置在一栋看似医院或学校的建筑物内。该建筑共有17或18个房间，每个房间住有60多名苦力，并由一名日本士兵看守。2月18日下午3时，我们被告知离开该建筑，沿原路返回码头。

当我们从南通城墙前往南通天生港码头的途中，一名日本军官询问我们是否为上海本地人。

It was ascertained that I and eleven others were natives
of Shanghai. We were then separated from the others
and told to stand in a field. As it was evening, we
were sent back to the same building in the Nantung City
where we passed the second night. We were not given
any supper. At 6 a.m., February 19, we, twelve
Shanghai coolies went, on our own initiative, to the
wharf at Tien Sun Kong, but no boat could be found.
At the suggestion of the Chinese policemen there, we
passed the third night and the subsequent nights in a
temple near the wharf. The Chinese policemen gave us
**〔此处转录不清〕** We stayed in the temple until February
22 when **〔此处转录不清〕** arty left for Shanghai on the s.s.
"Nantung", whilst I and the nine other coolies left for Shanghai
during the evening by **〔此处转录不清〕** her steamer, name unknown.
We purchased our own **〔此处转录不清〕** tickets at $3.80 each.
Those who had no money were obliged to pledge their
clothing with the steamer employees.

On arrival at 8 a.m., February 23, the ship
berthed at Pootung, opposite Dalny Road. I then returned
to my home by crossing the Whangpoo in a sampan.

I and the eleven other coolies, who are natives
of Shanghai, were conscripted on February 16 and released
on February 22. We were not paid for our services. We
were fed with nothing more than Shantung cakes and cooked
rice.

(Signed) Pan Kung Di.

- 3 -

经查明，我及另外十一人均为上海籍人士。随后我们与其他人员分开，并被命令在一片空地上站立。由于当时已是傍晚，我们被送回南通城同一座建筑内，在那里度过了第二夜。我们未获供应任何晚餐。2月19日上午6时，我们十二名上海苦力自行前往天生港码头，但未能找到船只。根据在场中国警察的建议，我们在码头附近的一座庙宇中度过了第三夜及随后的几夜。中国警察给了我们**〔此处转录不清〕**。我们在庙中停留至2月22日，当时**〔此处转录不清〕**一行人乘坐“南通”号轮船前往上海，而我与另外九名苦力则于当晚搭乘**〔此处转录不清〕**另一艘轮船（船名不详）前往上海。我们自行购买了**〔此处转录不清〕**船票，每张票价3.80元。那些身无分文的人被迫将衣物抵押给轮船雇员。

2月23日上午8时抵达后，船舶停泊在浦东大连路对面。随后我乘舢板渡过黄浦江返回家中。

我及另外十一名同为上海籍的苦力于2月16日被征用，并于2月22日获释。我们的服务未获任何报酬。我们所获食物仅有山东饼和熟米饭。

（签名）潘公迪

February 16th, 1942.

Mr. D. E. Harbottle.

Sir,

I beg to report that one Ordure Coolie (No.799), one
Daily Latrine Coolie (No.1207) and two Sweeping Coolies
(Nos. 1200 & 1243) were commandeered by a Japanese Military
detachment this morning when they were at work in Yangtzepoo
Road near Sunkan Road at about 5.30.

Enquiries made at the Japanese Gendarmerie Station in
Pingliang Road, elicited the information that the commandeering
of labour was completed this morning and that the labour
commandeered has already left this city for a certain place
this morning.

It was stated that the labour will be sent back to this
city in due course.

(Sgd.) K. Fujita.

/TPN

一九四二年二月十六日。

先生：

谨此报告，一名清粪苦力（第799号）、一名日常厕所苦力（第1207号）及两名清扫苦力（第1200号及1243号），于今晨约五时三十分在杨树浦路靠近孙家宅路（Sunkan Road）处工作时，被一支日军分队征用。

经向平凉路日本宪兵队查询，获悉征用劳工之事已于今晨办妥，且被征用之劳工已于今晨离开本市前往某地。

据称，该等劳工将在适当时候遣回本市。

（签名）K. Fujita。

February 19th, 1941.

Mr. D. E. Herbottle,
Sir,
    I beg to report that Officer i/c the Japanese Gendarmerie Station in Pingliang Road yesterday requested me, through Yulin Road Police Station, to furnish him with information regarding the living condition of the families of those P.W.D. Coolies who were commandeered by a Japanese detachment on the 10th inst., so that he may report details to the Japanese Army Headquarters in order to relieve the difficulty of those families. He stated that he would let us know as soon as he receives a reply from the Headquarters.
    Therefore, I gave him the following information:-
Latrine coolie No. 1207.
    Name: Sung Cheung Soon (宋章順).
    Age: 49.
    Address: 123 Lou Ven Teh Lee, Point Rd.
    Native place: Eiecheng, Kiangsu.
    Wife's name: Sung Pan Sz (宋潘氏).
    Her age: 37.

Misc. 21/41.
Yangtsepoo 8039A/42
(5) Feb. 27th, 41.

Japanese Military Press Gangs Operating in Yangtsepoo District.

D.S.I. Smith

Sir,

On the 24/2/41 Mr. K. Fujita, Inspector, S.M.C.
P.W.D. Antung Road Depot, reported that three of the
four P.W.D. coolies who were seized by Japanese
Military Press Gangs on the 16/2/41 had returned to
work.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

1. Sung Chaung Soong (申長松), age 49 years, native
of Kompo, M/P.W.D. Coolie No. 1207, residing
at No. ? Lane 201 Tsu Ka Ba Road.

2. Chang Sung Kun (張生坤), age 57 years, native
of Shanghai, M/P.W.D. Coolie No. 1243, residing
at 72 E Zung Li off Yangtsepoo Road.

3. Pan Kung Di (潘根弟) alias Lee Mou Ling (李茂林)
age 48 years, native of Ninghai, M/P.W.D. Coolie
No. 1200, residing at No. 127 Dong Ho Li off
Glen Road.

The three coolies when questioned by detectives
made similar statements to the effect that after they
were seized on Yangtsepoo Road, early on the morning
of the 16/2/41 they together with about 10 other coolies
were given boxes of ammunition to carry and marched to
the Jukong Wharf, Woosung, and put with a gang of about
60 other Chinese coolies.

At 10 a.m. on the 16/2/41 the coolies were placed
on board boats and taken to Tien Sung Kong (天生港)
arriving there about 10 a.m. on the 17/2/41 when they
unloaded boxes of ammunition from the boats and later
carried them across country to Nantung where they stayed
in school and hospital buildings until the afternoon of

杂项 21/41。
杨树浦 8039A/42
(5) 1941年2月27日。

日军在杨树浦区活动的强征劳工队。

史密斯副督察

先生：

1941年2月24日，工部局工务处安通路堆栈督察藤田（K. Fujita）先生报告称，在1941年2月16日被日军强征劳工队抓走的四名工务处苦力中，已有三人返回工作岗位。

（印：特科）

1. 申长松（Sung Chaung Soong），49岁，高邮（Kompo）人，工务处苦力编号1207，住曹家坝路201弄?号。

2. 张生坤（Chang Sung Kun），57岁，上海人，工务处苦力编号1243，住杨树浦路荣里东72号。

3. 潘根弟（Pan Kung Di），又名李茂林（Lee Mou Ling），48岁，宁海人，工务处苦力编号1200，住格伦路（Glen Road）东何里127号。

这三名苦力在接受侦探讯问时作了类似的陈述，大意是：他们在1941年2月16日清晨于杨树浦路被抓后，与其他约十名苦力一起被分发弹药箱搬运，并被押往吴淞的菊宫码头（Jukong Wharf），与另外约60名中国苦力汇合。

1941年2月16日上午10时，这些苦力被带上船，运往天生港（Tien Sung Kong），于1941年2月17日上午10时左右抵达。他们从船上卸下弹药箱，随后陆路搬运至南通，在学校和医院建筑物内停留，直到当天下午

page_data.en:
-2-

the 18/2/41.
At 4 p.m. 18/2/41 the coolies were assembled
and ordered to carry the ammunition, brought from
Shanghai, to a large field adjacent to the North
Gate at Nantung City. At 6 p.m. 18/2/41 the
impressed coolies from Shanghai were informed that
they were at liberty to return home via Tien Sung Kong
where steamer passage would be provided for them.
They eventually arrived at Shanghai on February 22nd
and 23rd 1941 respectively.
Statements attached.

D.D.O. "D"

Copy to O. i/c S.B.

J. Smith
D. S. I.

1941年2月18日。
1941年2月18日下午4时，苦力们被集合起来，奉命将自上海运来的弹药搬运至南通城北门附近的一片大空地。1941年2月18日下午6时，来自上海的征用苦力获知，他们可经天生港（Tien Sung Kong）自由返家，当局将为它们提供轮船舱位。他们最终分别于1941年2月22日和23日抵达上海。

page_data.en:
Sung Cheung Soong (宋昌松).
C.M.C. 298
translated
Clerk Chen Fu Keng

My name is Sung Cheung Soong, age 49 years, native of
Kompo, S.M.C. garbage coolie No. 1207, residing at No. 7
Lane 201 You Ka Ba Road.

At about 5.30 a.m. 16/2/41, I left my home to report for
work at the Autung Food Depot. I walked from East to West
along Yangtzepoo Road and when near the Kwangshin Road
intersection, I was stopped by one of Japanese soldiers who
were coming from the opposite direction. The soldier said
that he wanted me to carry some boxes of ammunition to Jukong
Wharf. I was given some ammunition to carry and together
with about 10 other coolies I was taken to Jukong Wharf where
I saw about 50 or 60 Chinese coolies and amongst them were
two men whom I recognized to be my fellow workers. At
about 10 a.m. 16/2/41 all of us were forced to board a lighter
and was given one rice-ball to eat. The lighter carried us
to Tien Sung Kong, Hongkew, where we stayed in a hospital
behind the City Government Building. At about 4 p.m.
16/2/41 we carried some ammunition to a field outside the
East Gate. At about 6 p.m. 16/2/41, a Japanese officer
came and told us that those who came from Shanghai should
raise hands. 12 men responded including myself. The
officer then said that we could return to Shanghai via Tien
Sung Kong without paying any steamer fare. We then went
to Tien Sung Kong ourselves but owing to the closure of the
harbour we had to stay there until 21/2/41 when a steamer
arrived which brought me to Shanghai. The steamer tied-up
at the Tungchow Wharf, Marche de l'Est, French Bund at about
12 m.n. 22/2/41. The above is my true statement.

Sd. Sung Chung Soong.
page_data.zh:
宋昌松。
C.M.C. 298
已翻译
书记员陈福庚

我叫宋昌松，49岁，籍贯高邮（Kompo），系工部局第1207号垃圾搬运夫，住于优卡巴路（You Ka Ba Road）201弄7号。

1941年2月16日上午5时30分左右，我离家前往奥通食品仓库（Autung Food Depot）报到上班。我沿杨树浦路由东向西行走，当行至广新路（Kwangshin Road）交叉口附近时，被一名迎面走来的日本士兵拦下。该士兵称要我帮忙搬运几箱弹药至朱公码头（Jukong Wharf）。我受命搬运一些弹药，并与其他约10名苦力一同被带往朱公码头，在那里我看见约有五六十名中国苦力，其中有两人为我认识的同事。1941年2月16日上午10时许，我们所有人被迫登上一艘驳船，每人分得一个饭团食用。驳船将我们载至虹口天同宫（Tien Sung Kong, Hongkew），我们栖身于市政府大楼后方的一家医院内。1941年2月16日下午4时许，我们将一些弹药搬运至东门外的田野处。1941年2月16日下午6时许，一名日本军官前来，告知从上海来的人举手。包括我在内的12人举了手。随后该军官表示，我们可以经天同宫返回上海，无需支付任何轮船费。于是我们自行前往天同宫，但因港口关闭，我们不得不滞留于此，直至1941年2月21日一艘轮船抵达，将我载回上海。该轮于1941年2月22日子夜12时许停靠在法外滩东方市场（Marche de l'Est）的通州码头（Tungchow Wharf）。以上陈述属实。

签署：宋昌松

My name is Chang Sung Kun, age 57 years, native of
Shanghai, S.M.C. garbage coolie No. 1243, residing at 72
B Tung Li off Yangtszepoo Road.

At about 5.30 a.m. 16/2/41, I left my home to report
for work at Antung Road Depot. When I was walking along
Yangtszepoo Road near Lincning Road I saw a number of Japanese
soldiers coming in the opposite direction. The Japanese
soldiers stopped me and said that they wanted me to carry
some boxes of ammunition to Jukong Wharf and that I would
be released after arriving there. One of the Japanese
soldiers then threw away a broom and my service vest which
I carried in my hands.

I carried the ammunition and followed the Japanese
soldiers to Jukong Wharf where I saw about 50 or 60 Chinese
coolies and amongst them were two men whom I recognized to be
my fellow workers. At about 10 a.m. 16/2/41 we were forced
to board a motor boat, which carried us to Tien Sung Kong,
Nantung. Whilst on the boat we were each given one rice-ball
to eat. We arrived at Tien Sung Kong at about 10 a.m. on
the 17/2/41 when we all went ashore and were taken to stay
in the premises of a school for the night and at about 4 p.m.
18/2/41 we were ordered to carry ammunition to a field outside
the North Gate where a Japanese officer told us in Chinese
language that those who came from Shanghai should raise hands.
12 men responded including myself. The officer again said
that we could return to Shanghai via Tien Sung Kong without
paying any steamer fare. After which we were allowed to

张松坤（〔此处转录不清〕），
上海，                                     职员陈福庚，
杨树浦路，          1941年2月24日，      翻译   陈职员
                                             xxxx

我叫张松坤，57岁，上海人，系上海公共租界工部局第1243号垃圾清运苦力，现居住于杨树浦路旁东里72号。

1941年2月16日上午5时30分左右，我离开家前往安东路车场报到上班。当我沿杨树浦路走近临清路时，看见数名日本士兵迎面走来。日本士兵拦住我，说他们要我搬运几箱弹药至菊功码头，并称到达那里后就会释放我。随后，一名日本士兵扔掉了扫帚和我手中拿着的工作背心。

我搬运着弹药，跟随日本士兵来到菊功码头，在那里我看见约有五六十名中国苦力，其中有两人名我认出是我的同事。1941年2月16日上午10时左右，我们被迫登上一艘摩托艇，该船将我们载往南通的天生港。在船上时，每人分得一个饭团食用。我们于1941年2月17日上午10时左右抵达天生港，随后全体上岸，被带至一所学校的房舍内过夜。1941年2月18日下午4时左右，我们奉命将弹药搬运至北门外的一处空地，一名日本军官用中文告诉我们，凡是从上海来的人请举手。包括我在内有12人响应。该军官又说，我们可以经天生港返回上海，无需支付任何轮船费用。此后，我们获准

page_data.en:
-2-

walk to Tien Sung Kong ourselves, and on arriving there
we were again stopped by some Japanese civilians who asked
us to load and discharge cargo from the trucks and boats
at the wharf.
Owing to the closure of the harbour we stayed in a
temple and worked for the Japanese civilians who gave us
food regularly until 22/2/41 when a steamer arrived and
by which we returned to Shanghai. The steamer arrived
at Tatung (Tungchow) wharf, **〔此处转录不清〕** at about 8 a.m. 23/2/41.
The above is my true statement.

Signed Chang Sung Kun
page_data.zh:
-2-

我们自行步行前往天盛公（Tien Sung Kong），抵达那里后，再次被几名日本平民拦下，他们要求我们在码头将货物从卡车和船上装卸。
由于港口关闭，我们住在一座寺庙里，为那些定期提供食物的日本平民做工，直到1941年2月22日一艘轮船抵达，我们便乘该船返回上海。该轮于1941年2月23日上午8时左右抵达大通（通州）码头，**〔此处转录不清〕**。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名：张松坤（Chang Sung Kun）

Misc. 23/41.

(4) Yangtsepoo
Feb. 21, 8039P/ 41.
Japanese Military Press Gangs Operating in Yangtsepoo District.

D. S. I. Smith

Sir,

At 10 a.m. 21/2/41 Mr. F. H. Watson, Chief Inspector,
S. M. C./P. W. D. Highways Department, came to this station
accompanied by two coolies named below whom he stated
were seized by a Japanese Military Press Gang at Yang-
tsepoo Road near Sungpan Road Market at 7.30 a.m. on
the 14/2/41.

1. Kyung Yue Chi ( 金方池 ), age 43 years, Kompo,
M/P.W.D. Coolie No.524, 58 Loong Yi Li ( 龍義里 ),
Yangtsepoo Road.

2. Tso Ng Zeh Ts ( 祝五子 ), age 19 years, Taichow,
S/P.W.D. Coolie No.514, No.10 Soong Yang Li,
( 宋陽里 ) Wuchow Road.

The two coolies state that whilst they were walking
along Yangtsepoo Road near Sungpan Road Market at about
7.30 a.m. on the 14/2/41 they were seized by Japanese
soldiers and forcibly taken to the Wing On Textile
Manufacturing Co., No.1570 Yangtsepoo Road, where they
were issued with a yellow armlet and placed among three
or four hundred other coolies in a 1st floor room of
the premises. The majority of these coolies they learned
had been seized by the Japanese Military authorities
at various towns on the Shanghai Hangchow Railway.

At 4 a.m. 15/2/41 the coolies were assembled in the
compound at No.1570 Yangtsepoo Road and given a box of
ammunition to carry, then marched under escort to the
Shanghai North Railway Station. After stacking the
ammunition in the compound at the station Kyung Yue Chi
( 金方池 ) and Tso Ng Zeh Ts ( 祝五子 ) state that they
removed their armlets and managed to escape.

Statements attached.

D. S. I.
J. Smith

D. D. O. "D"

D. S. I. 史密斯

先生：

1941年2月21日上午10时，工部局警务处公共工程部道路股总督察 F. H. 沃森先生来到本警署，随同前来的有下述两名苦力。据称，他们于1941年2月14日上午7时30分在杨树浦路近宋潘路市场处被日军强征队抓走。

1. 金方池 (Kyung Yue Chi)，43岁，籍贯高邮 (Kompo)，公共工程部苦力编号524，住址杨树浦路龙义里58号。

2. 祝五子 (Tso Ng Zeh Ts)，19岁，籍贯泰州 (Taichow)，公共工程部苦力编号514，住址梧州路宋阳里10号。

两名苦力称，1941年2月14日上午7时30分左右，当他们行走在杨树浦路近宋潘路市场处时，被日本士兵抓住，并强行带至杨树浦路1570号永安纺织制造公司。在那里，他们被发给黄色臂章，并被安置在该楼房二楼的一个房间内，与其他三四百名苦力关在一起。他们得知，这些苦力大多是被日本军方当局在上海至杭州铁路沿线的各个城镇抓来的。

1941年2月15日凌晨4时，苦力们在杨树浦路1570号的院子里集合，每人分发一箱弹药携带，随后在押送下步行前往上海北站。在车站院内堆放好弹药后，金方池和祝五子称，他们摘掉臂章，设法逃脱。

附供词。

D. S. I.
J. 史密斯

page_data.en:
Kyung Yue Chi,
Kaoyue, Kompo, C.D.C. 307
Y'poo Stn., 21/2/41, translated xxxxx Clerk Shen Pei Ying

My name is Kyung Yue Chi, age 43 years, M/P.W.D. Highway
Coolie No. 524, native of Kaoyue, Kompo, residing at No. 58
Loong Yi Li, Pingliang Road. I have been working as a
Highway Coolie more than 10 years. At 6 a.m. 14/2/41 I
left my home and went to report for work at the Sawgin Road
Depot. At 7 a.m. even date I was detailed together with
11 others to work at the corner of Yangtszepoo and Kueiyang
Roads. We proceeded to the above place via Yalu Road, Point
Road, Muirhead Road and Yangtszepoo Road. 10 of these
coolies went away to take their breakfast whilst I together
with Tso Ng Zeh Ts (P.W.D. Highway Coolie No. 514) continued
our journey to the aforementioned place and on approaching
the Sungpan Road market we encountered six Japanese soldiers,
two standing on one side of the road and the rest on the
opposite side, who stopped and took us together with eight
others to the Wing On Cotton Mill godown on Yangtszepoo Road,
where on the 1st floor we met about 3 or 4 hundred male
Chinese who had also been forcibly taken there by Japanese
soldiers. Each of us was issued with a length of yellow
cloth which the Japanese soldier ordered to be tied around
the right arm. At the tiffin time we were each given a
handful of rice. During the night I heard from others
that some of them had been brought there from Pinghu and some
from Kating. At 4 a.m. 15/2/41 we were escorted to the
North Railway Station arriving there at about 6 a.m. when
after having unloaded the ammunition case which we had carried
on our person I together with Tso Ng Zeh Ts and three other
unknown persons took away the armlet and managed to escape
from the Japanese soldiers. The above is my true statement.
Sd. Kyung Yue Chi.
page_data.zh:
Kyung Yue Chi，
高邮，甘泉，C.D.C. 307
杨树浦站，1941年2月21日，由书记员沈佩英翻译 xxxxx

我叫 Kyung Yue Chi，43岁，工务局道路苦力，编号524，籍贯高邮、甘泉，现居平凉路龙义里58号。我从事道路苦力工作已逾十年。1941年2月14日上午6时，我离家前往萨金路（Sawgin Road）堆栈报到上班。同日早上7时，我与另外11人被派往杨树浦路与贵阳路转角处工作。我们经由鸭绿江路、波恩特路（Point Road）、穆黑德路（Muirhead Road）和杨树浦路前往上述地点。其中10名苦力离开去吃早餐，而我与 Tso Ng Zeh Ts（工务局道路苦力，编号514）继续前往上述地点。在接近松潘路市场时，我们遇到了六名日本士兵，两人站在路的一侧，其余站在对面。他们拦住我们，并将我们连同另外八人带至杨树浦路上的永安纱厂仓库。在一楼，我们见到了约三四百名同样被日本士兵强行带至此处的中国男子。我们每个人都被发给一段黄布，日本士兵命令将其系在右臂上。午餐时间，我们每人得到一把米。夜间，我从其他人那里听说，他们中有些人是从平湖带来的，有些是从嘉定（Kating）带来的。1941年2月15日凌晨4时，我们被护送至北站，约于上午6时抵达。在卸下我们随身携带的弹药箱后，我与 Tso Ng Zeh Ts 及另外三名身份不明者取下臂章，设法从日本士兵手中逃脱。以上是我的真实陈述。
签名：Kyung Yue Chi

Tso Ng Zeh Ts,
Taichow, Kompo,                                     C.D.C. 307
Y'poo Stn.,           21-2-41,          Translated
                                            xxxx      Clerk Shen Pei Ying

My name is Tso Ng Zeh Ts, age 19 years, S/P.W.D. Highway
Coolie No. 514, native of Taichow, Kompo, residing at No. 10
Soong Yeng Li, Wuchow Road.    I have been working as a Highway
Coolie more than two years.    At about 6.30 a.m. 14/2/41 I
went to report for work at the Sawgin Road Depot and was
detailed together with 11 others to work at the corner of
Yangtszepoo and Kueiyang Roads.    I together with Coolie
No. 524 Kyung Yue Chi proceeded to the aforementioned place
via Yalu Road, Point Road, Muirhead Road and Yangtszepoo Road
and on approaching the Sungpan Road market, the time being
at about 7.30 a.m., we encountered six Japanese soldiers
standing on both sides of the road.    They stopped and took
us to the Wing On Cotton Mill godown on Yangtszepoo Road
where they issued us with a length of yellow cloth which
they ordered to be tied around the right arm.    We were
kept on the 1st floor where we met 3 or 4 hundred male Chinese
who had also been taken by Japanese soldiers.    At the tiffin
time we were each given a handful of rice.    At 4 a.m. the
next day (15/2/41) we were escorted to the North Railway
Station arriving there at about 6 a.m.    After having unloaded
the ammunition case which we had carried on our person we took
away the armlet and managed to escape during the absence of
the Japanese soldiers.    The above is my true statement.
                                Signed. Tso Ng Zeh Ts.

江苏泰州，                                     C.D.C. 307

                                            xxxx      书记员 沈佩英

我叫曹五泽茨（音译），19岁，系工部局道路处第514号苦力，籍贯江苏泰州，现居住于梧州路松英里10号。我担任道路苦力已有两年多。1941年2月14日上午6时30分左右，我前往沙金路堆栈报到上班，并与另外11人一起被派往杨树浦路与贵阳路转角处工作。我与第524号苦力邝月池（音译）经由鸭绿江路、波因特路（Point Road）、穆黑德路（Muirhead Road）和杨树浦路前往上述地点，大约在上午7时30分接近松潘路市场时，我们遇到六名日本士兵站在道路两侧。他们拦住我们，将我们带到杨树浦路上的永安纱厂仓库，在那里发给我们每人一段黄布，命令我们绑在右臂上。我们被关在二楼，在那里遇到了三四百名同样被日本士兵抓来的中国男子。午饭时间，我们每人分到一把米。次日（1941年2月15日）凌晨4时，我们被护送至北站，约于上午6时抵达。在卸下我们随身携带的弹药箱后，我们取下了臂章，并趁日本士兵不在时设法逃脱。以上是我的真实陈述。
                                签名：曹五泽茨（音译）。

侦探在杨树浦路近松潘路处进行调查，找到一名叫陈荣昌（Zung Yoong Tsang）的人，系杨树浦路1825弄雇用的私人更夫，他目睹了张生坤（Chang Sung Kun）于1941年2月16日上午被日本士兵强行带走。

February 16th, 1941.

Mr. D. E. Harbottle.

Sir,
    I beg to report that one Ordure Coolie No. 789)
one Daily Latrine Coolie (No. 1207) and two Sweeping
Coolies (Nos. 1200 and 1243) were commandeered by a
Japanese military detachment this morning when they
were at work in Yangtsepoo Road near Sungpan Road at

    Enquiries made at the Japanese Gendarmerie Station
in Pingliang Road, elicited the information that the
commandeering of labour was completed this morning and
that the labour commandeered has already left this
city for a certain place this morning.
    It was stated that the labour will be sent back to

                                Sd. Fujita.

Misc. 49/41.
Yulin Road
February 20th 41.

Male Chinese Missing.

D.I. Shields.

Sir,
I beg to report that at 3.40 p.m. 20-2-41, a
female Chinese named Tsang Zung Sz (張陳氏) age 45,
native of Ningpo, residing at 300 Yulin Road came to
this station and reported that while she and her husband
named Tsang San Loong (張三龍), age 54, native of
Ningpo, height 5'6", wearing blue short jacket and pants
a fitter No. 64 employed by the Yoong Shing Iron Factory
a Japanese concern situated at 731-9 Pingliang Road, were
walking on Jansen Road near Yulin Road at 7.45 p.m.
15-2-41, four Japanese dressed in Kahki uniforms seized
her husband by the arms and forced him into a waiting,
yellow painted motor lorry which was already laden with
about 40 male Chinese, the m/lorry then drove off North
towards Kinchow Road. Since then her husband has not
been seen.
The informant made representations to the above firm
on Sunday morning 16-2-41 and they telephoned to some
Japanese Military Office but could get no satisfactory
reply. She then made enquiries throughout the Eastern
without result.
Her son, Tsang En Woo, age 28, is charged from this
station with Armed Robbery and it was while she was
visiting him that the above information was obtained.
D.S. Suga has communicated the particulars of the
missing man to the Japanese Gendarme 250 Pingliang Road.
Forwarded for information.
D.D.O."D" and CD.I. Tabrun informed.
Statement attached.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

杂项 49/41。
榆林路
1941年2月20日。

中国男子失踪。

警司希尔德斯（Shields）。

先生，
谨此报告，1941年2月20日下午3时40分，一名名为张陈氏（Tsang Zung Sz）的中国女性，45岁，宁波籍，居住于榆林路300号，来到本警署报案称：1941年2月15日晚上7时45分，当她和其丈夫张三龙（Tsang San Loong，54岁，宁波籍，身高5英尺6英寸，身穿蓝色短夹克和长裤，系受雇于位于平凉路731-9号的日本企业永兴铁厂的第64号钳工）在榆林路附近的詹森路（Jansen Road）行走时，四名身穿卡其色制服的日本人抓住她丈夫的双臂，强行将他塞进一辆等候着的、漆成黄色的机动卡车，该卡车当时已载有约40名中国男子，随后卡车向北驶往锦州路（Kinchow Road）方向。自此之后，其丈夫便下落不明。
报案人于1941年2月16日（星期日）上午向上述工厂提出交涉，厂方致电某日本军方机构，但未得到满意答复。随后她在东区各处查询，均无结果。
其子张恩武（Tsang En Woo），28岁，正由本警署以持械抢劫罪起诉，上述信息系她在探视其子期间获得。
须贺（Suga）警佐已将失踪者的详细情况通报给位于平凉路250号的日本宪兵队。
呈报供参考。
已通知“D”区副警务总监及华人总探长塔布伦（Tabrun）。

Tsang Sung Sz, age 45, M/Female, residing
at 300 Yulin Road.
Ningpo. C.D.C. 348.
Y.Rd. Stn. 20-8-41. translated Clerk Teng Pah Chun.
xxxxxx

At about 7 p.m., 16-8-41, I together with my husband named
Tsang San Loong, age 54, Ningpo, went to a rice shop, address
unknown, but situated on Baikal Road. However, we both returned
on account of the high price of the rice. On the way home, as
we passed Jansen Road near Yulin Road, we saw a yellow painted
motor truck driving South to North along Jansen Road at a high
speed. It suddenly stopped when it was near us. Four unarmed men
all dressed in yellow kahki uniform then came down from the
truck. Two of them men then dragged my husband to the truck, and
forced him up into same. The truck then carried them all away
in a Southern direction along Jansen Road, the time then being
about quarter to eight. In the meantime I saw that there were
about forty other male Chinese on the truck.

Cross signed.
Tsang Zung Sz.

1941年8月16日晚7时许，我与丈夫曾三龙（Tsang San Loong，54岁，宁波人）前往一家米店，地址不详，但位于贝加尔路（Baikal Road）。然而，因米价高昂，我们二人随即返回。在回家途中，当我们经过靠近榆林路的詹森路（Jansen Road）时，看见一辆漆成黄色的摩托卡车沿詹森路由南向北高速行驶。当车驶近我们时，突然停下。随后，四名未携带武器、均身着黄色卡其制服的男子从卡车上下来。其中两人将我丈夫拖至卡车旁，并强行将其推上车。随后，卡车载着他们所有人沿詹森路向南驶去，当时时间约为七点四十五分。在此期间，我看见卡车上还有约四十名其他中国男子。

FED 2

Japanese Probe Report
“Press Gang”
Work Done
By Contractors

Japanese military authorities
yesterday blamed Chinese labor
contractors for disappearance of
laborers in connection with re-
ports that Japanese army “press
gangs” were in operation in the
northern areas of the Settle-
ment:

An investigation was carried out
by the Japanese authorities, accord-
ing to a Japanese official, and it
was learned that no one was forced
into labor. The Chinese contractors
who are hired by the Japanese army,
contract men from whom they get
a commission, when work is found.
These men are sent to a certain
depot, according to the official, and
are taken to work.

In their greed for gain, the
official said, the contractors recruit
unemployed men off the streets, and
sometimes they gather men who
are not of the labor class. These
men, the official went on to say, re-
fuse to work when they are set to
it, and the Japanese sentries, who
stand guard over them, sometimes
do not understand Chinese. This
results in friction, and when the
men escape, as they often do as
these places are not strongly guard-
ed, they make anti-Japanese state-
ments.

No force is used by the Japanese
army to persuade these men to
work, and what force is used comes
from the Chinese contractors them-
selves, who desire to make more
money.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

FED 2

日本方面调查报告
“抓壮丁”
承包商所为

日本军方当局
昨日将劳工失踪一事归咎于中国劳工
承包商，此前有报告称日本军队在公共租界
北部地区活动“抓壮丁”：

据一名日本官员称，日本当局已展开
调查，并获悉无人被强迫劳动。受雇于日军的
中国承包商，从其所招募的人员身上抽取佣金，
一旦找到工作机会，便将这些人员送往某一
集散地，据该官员称，随后他们被带往工地做工。

该官员表示，承包商出于贪利之心，从街头招募
失业男子，有时甚至聚集非劳工阶层的人员。
该官员接着说，这些人被安排工作时往往拒绝
劳动，而看守他们的日本哨兵有时不懂中文。这
导致摩擦产生，而当这些人逃跑时——由于这些
地方守卫并不严密，逃跑情况经常发生——他们
便发表反日言论。

日军并未使用武力迫使这些人劳动，所使用的
任何强制手段均来自中国承包商自身，他们意在
赚取更多钱财。

（印：特别科）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
West Hongkew Station, REGISTRY
No. S. P. D. 863 / 9
Date March 9th, 1940

Subject North r to male Chinese taken away by the Japanese Naval Authorities.

Made by D. S. Rhodes. Forwarded by Inspector,
Officer i/c

Sir,

Since Ying Ching Woo (殷金保) was forcibly removed from his home at 253 North Kiangse Road by a Japanese Marine, detectives have daily continued to visit his home and on March 9th, 1940, it was learned that he had returned.

At the request of the Police Ying attended West Hongkew Station where he gave a voluntary statement regarding his arrest and subsequent detention by the Japanese Garrison at the North Railway Station. (Copy of statement attached).

As will be seen by reference to the initial report on this subject, the information which led to Ying's arrest was passed to the Japanese Authorities primarily through the chief tenant of No. 253 North Kiangse Road one Tsah Dah Zung (蔡大振) who appears to have greatly enlarged upon the supposed incident which was alleged to have befallen Ying in Hongkew on the morning of March 5th, 1940.

However it should be mentioned that the chief tenant was formerly employed by the Japanese Naval Authorities in the pass issuing office, and thus this exaggerated report may have been made for the purpose of personal gain.

Ying states that on the morning of 5-3-40 whilst in Hongkew enroute to work, he heard from various people, reports that able bodied men were being pressed into service by the Japanese Authorities.

This report had the effect of compelling him to return home where he commented to the chief tenant of the rumours he had heard.. The remarks of Ying then appear to have been relayed to the Japanese Garrison through Cong Ching Sung.

（左侧边缘手写批注及印章）：

报告

杂项档案号 96/40
上海公共租界工部局警务处
虹口西区捕房，登记处
编号 S. P. D. 863 / 9
日期 1940年3月9日

事由 关于一名中国男子被日本海军当局带走的报告。

制作人：D. S. Rhodes。经由督察、主管警官转呈。

先生：

自殷金保（Ying Ching Woo）在江西路北路253号住所被一名日本海军陆战队士兵强行带走后，侦探每日持续前往其住所探访，并于1940年3月9日获悉其已返回。

应警方要求，殷某前往虹口西区捕房，就其在北站被日本驻军逮捕及随后拘留一事作了自愿陈述。（陈述副本附后）。

如查阅本案的初步报告所示，导致殷某被捕的情报主要是由江西路北路253号的主要租客蔡大振（Tsah Dah Zung）传递给日本当局的；此人似乎极大地夸大了据称于1940年3月5日上午发生在虹口的涉及殷某的所谓事件。

然而，必须指出的是，该主要租客此前曾在日本海军当局的通行证签发办公室任职，因此这份夸张的报告可能是为了个人利益而编造的。

殷某称，1940年3月5日上午，他在虹口上班途中，从多人处听到传闻，称日本当局正在强征身强力壮的男子服役。

这一传闻促使他返回家中，并向主要租客评论了他所听到的谣言。殷某的言论随后似乎通过 Cong Ching Sung（音译）转达给了日本驻军。

（左侧边缘手写批注及印章）：
归档
日期 13/3

Ying stoutly denies that he was held up and bound by
Japanese and Chinese civilians and avers that he made no
mention of same to his chief tenant.

His interrogation whilst in the hands of the Japanese
Garrison appears to have been in connection with his alleged
circulation of unfounded rumours.

There is every reason to believe the account of the
incident as related by Ying, since he does not appear to be
afraid to tell details.

Enquiries have failed to secure any concrete evidence to
show that press gangs are operating, this case is undoubtedly
an enquiry by the Japanese re alleged abduction of Chinese.

英（Ying）坚决否认曾被日本及中国平民拦截并捆绑，并声称他未曾向其主租户提及此事。

他在日本驻军拘押期间所受的讯问，似乎与他涉嫌散布不实谣言有关。

鉴于英（Ying）并不避讳陈述细节，我们有充分理由相信他所叙述的事件经过属实。

经调查，未能获取任何确凿证据以表明存在强征壮丁的行为；本案无疑系日方就所谓绑架中国人一事所进行的调查。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Ying Ching Hoo
native of Tungchow taken by me D.S. Rhodes and C.D.C. 255
W.H. Stn. on the 9-3-40 and interpreted by Interpreter Tao.

My name is Ying Ching Hoo, 26, native of Tungchow,
M/mason, residing at No. 253 North Kiangse Road.

Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in August 1937, I was employed as a mason by one Wong Boh
Ching who at that time operated a small contractors business
at Boone Road.

In August 1939 through the introduction of a friend I
obtained employment with a Japanese owned building contractor
and daily carried out work in the Hongkew area.

On March 3rd 1940 I took up residence at No. 253 North
Kiangse Road.

At about 8 a.m. March 5th 1940 I left home with the
intention of proceeding to Chungshan Road to continue my
employment. Upon arriving in the vicinity of North Szechuen
Road near Kanle Road I heard several persons commenting on how
the Japanese Army Authorities were forcing able bodied Chinese
males into service.

Fearing that I may be arrested by the supposed press gangs
I returned home and mentioned to the chief tenant the
rumours I had heard regarding Chinese being pressed into service
by the Japanese.

I remained at home during the remainder of the day until
about 2 p.m. 5-3-40 when a male Chinese wearing foreign style
clothes accompanied by my chief tenant entered my room.

The male Chinese now known to me as Oong employed by the
Japanese Garrison picked up my pass from the table and asked
my name, etc, afterwards he left taking the pass away with him.

警务调查报告。

以下为通州籍人士 Ying Ching Hoo（音译）之陈述，由本人 D.S. Rhodes 及 C.D.C. 255 W.H. Stn. 于 1940 年 3 月 9 日录取，并由陶翻译员传译。

本人姓名 Ying Ching Hoo（音译），26 岁，通州人，职业泥瓦匠，住江西路北路 253 号。

在 1937 年 8 月中日战事爆发前，本人受雇于 Wong Boh Ching（音译）担任泥瓦匠，此人当时在 Boone Road（音译）经营一家小型承包商行。

1939 年 8 月，经朋友介绍，本人受雇于一家日资建筑承包商，每日在虹口地区做工。

1940 年 3 月 3 日，本人迁居至江西路北路 253 号。

1940 年 3 月 5 日上午 8 时许，本人离家，拟前往中山路继续工作。当抵达靠近康乐路的四川北路附近时，本人听到数人议论日本军方当局如何强征身强力壮的中国男子服役。

因担心可能被所谓的抓伕队逮捕，本人返回家中，并向二房东提及所听到的关于日本人强征中国人服役的谣言。

当日余下时间本人均留在家中，直至 1940 年 3 月 5 日下午 2 时许，一名身穿西式服装的中国男子随同本人的二房东进入本人房间。

该中国男子现知悉名为 Oong（音译），受雇于日本卫戍司令部，他从桌上拿起本人的通行证，询问了本人的姓名等情况，随后携带通行证离开。

page_data.en:
FORM 40
G. 44M 1-39

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of ........................................ ( 2 )
native of ........................................ taken by me........................................
........................................on the........................................ and interpreted by........................................

After Oong had left the premises I went to the downstairs front
room of the house and enquired of the chief tenant who the
person was who had taken my pass away.

A few minutes later Oong returned to 253 North Kiangse Road
whilst I was talking with the chief tenant, he was accompanied
by an armed Japanese Marine who speaking to me in Japanese
which I understood, accused me of being an undesirable individual
Oong then caught hold of my arm and attempted to force me to
accompany him and when I refused the Japanese Marine assisted
by threatening me with his rifle.

Arriving at the North Kiangse Road and Boone Road barrier,
Oong called a Japanese civilian who was standing near by, and
together they took me to the North Railway Station. The Japanese
remained at the North Kiangse Road barrier and the journey to
the North Station was made on foot, all the time Oong held me
by the wrist.

Arriving at the North Station Building I was escorted into an
office and there questioned by the Japanese Civilian and Oong
regarding my profession, etc. Afterwards I was confined in a
small room. During the afternoon of March 6th 1940, I was
removed from my cell and taken to a room and there a Japanese
Marine assisted by the Japanese civilian and Oong subjected me
to a rigid questioning regarding rumours of Japanese press gang,
which my interrogators accused me of having circulated.

After over one hour of questioning and electric torture I
was returned to my cell, and remained there until about 3 p.m.
8-3-40 when my wife arrived at the Japanese Garrison Headquarters

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为本人 ____ 于 ____ 对 ____ （2）
籍贯 ____ 之人士所作的问话记录，并由 ____ 担任翻译

在 Oong 离开该处所后，我前往该房屋楼下前厅，向主租客询问拿走我的通行证的人是谁。

几分钟后，当我正与主租客交谈时，Oong 返回江西路北路 253 号，他由一名武装日本海军陆战队士兵陪同，该士兵用日语对我说话（我能听懂），指责我是一个不受欢迎的人。随后 Oong 抓住我的手臂，试图强迫我随他同行，当我拒绝时，那名日本海军陆战队士兵用步枪威胁我，协助 Oong 强行带我走。

到达江西路北路与百老汇路（Boone Road）的关卡处，Oong 叫来一名站在附近的日本平民，他们一起将我带往北站。日本人留在江西路北路关卡处，前往北站的路程是步行完成的，在此期间 Oong 一直抓着我的手腕。

抵达北站大楼后，我被护送入一间办公室，并就我的职业等问题接受那名日本平民和 Oong 的讯问。之后，我被关在一间小房间里。1940 年 3 月 6 日下午，我被从牢房中带出，带到另一个房间，在那里，一名日本海军陆战队士兵在日本平民和 Oong 的协助下，就有关日军强征劳工队的谣言对我进行了严厉的讯问，审讯者指控这些谣言是由我散布的。

经过一个多小时的讯问和电刑折磨后，我被送回牢房，并一直待在那里，直到 1940 年 3 月 8 日下午 3 点左右，我的妻子抵达日本驻军司令部

At about 4.30 p.m. 8-3-40 I was taken to a room wherein

I was instructed that I was to be released and was

1940年3月8日下午4时30分左右，我被带进一个房间，里面有一名日本平民和几名日本海军陆战队士兵。

我被告知将被释放，并受到该日本平民的警告，不得向任何人透露我曾被捕一事；他还补充说，关于强征壮丁的谣言是虚假的，中国人被抓去只是做苦力，并非协助军队。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc. File No. 96/40
West Hongkew Station, 73
REPORT
Date March 5th, 1940

Subject Chinese male taken away by Japanese Naval Authorities.

Made by A. S. Hughes. Forwarded by Inspector,
Officer i/c

（左侧批注：P.A. File & add to file article in L.T.D. News of even date. R.W.H. 6/3.）

Sir,

At 4 p.m. 5-3-40, a report was received from P.S. 13
McCahey to the effect that at about 3.40 p.m. even date
he had observed a Japanese naval rating forcibly removing
a male Chinese from No. 953 North Kiangse Road, and
escorting him through the barrier situated at North
Kiangse Road and Boone Road corner.

Jap. Det. Ito, attached to Hongkew, C.I.D. 2nd and
the undersigned conducted enquiries and ascertained
the following details:-

According to one Tsai Dah Wai (蔡大振), chief
tenant of No. 953 North Kiangse Road, the person taken
away was one named:-

Yin Chin Foo (殷金福), aged about 21 years,
Tunchow, S/mason employed by an unknown Japanese
in the Hongkew district.

He only removed to the present address from Hongkew
on 4-3-40.

He added that at about 2.30 p.m. 5-3-40 Yin
mentioned to him how whilst on Boone Road in the
vicinity of Tonge Road during the forenoon 5-3-40 he
was accosted by a group of Japanese and Chinese civilians
who bound him with rope.

Before these men could remove him, Yin's employer
arrived on the scene and through his intervention he
was released.

At 3 p.m. 5-3-40 Tsah Dah Zung encountered one Wong
Ching Shing (翁振声) who he knew was employed by the
Japanese Garrison and to him he mentioned what Yin had
related to him regarding his escape in Hongkew.

（左侧方框内批注：Commr of Police Sir: I for info. R.W.H. D.C. (Sp. Br.) 6/3.）

（左下角手写：G.O.D. Sil E 6 3...）

杂项档案编号 96/40
虹口西区捕房，第73号
报告
日期：1940年3月5日

事由：一名中国男子被日本海军当局带走。

报告人：A. S. Hughes。经由警司、主管警官转呈

（左侧批注：政治档案。并将同日《字林西报》上的相关文章归入档案。R.W.H. 3月6日。）

先生：

1940年3月5日下午4时，收到第13巡捕房麦卡希（McCahey）的报告，称在当天下午约3时40分，他目睹一名日本海军士兵在北江西路953号强行带走一名中国男子，并押送其穿过位于北江西路与百老汇路（Boone Road）转角处的关卡。

隶属虹口刑事侦缉二股的日本侦探伊藤（Ito）与本报告人进行了调查，查明了以下细节：

据北江西路953号的主要租户蔡大振（Tsai Dah Wai）称，被带走者名为：

殷金福（Yin Chin Foo），年龄约21岁，通州人，石匠，受雇于虹口区一名身份不明的日本人。

他于1940年3月4日刚从虹口搬至现址。

他还补充说，1940年3月5日下午约2时30分，殷金福向他提及，当天上午他在百老汇路靠近唐吉路（Tonge Road）附近时，被一群日本和中国平民拦住，并用绳子将他捆绑。

就在这些人准备将他带走时，殷金福的雇主赶到现场，经其干预，殷金福得以释放。

1940年3月5日下午3时，蔡大振（此处原文拼写为 Tsah Dah Zung，疑为蔡大振之误）遇到翁振声（Wong Ching Shing），他知道翁振声受雇于日本驻军，于是便向翁振声讲述了殷金福之前向他所述的在虹口逃脱的经历。

（左侧方框内批注：警察总监 先生：我已知悉。R.W.H. 副总监（特务科）3月6日。）

The following is the statement of Tsah Dah Sung, age 23, M/caretaker, residing
at 253 North Kiangse Road. (Chief tenant)
native of Ningpo ........................................ taken by me ........................................
at W.H. Stn. .................... on the 5-3-40 .................... and interpreted by Interpreter Tao.

At about 10 a.m. 4-3-40, one Ying Ching Woo, a mason,
removed into my house. On the forenoon of 5-3-40, he went
to work in Hongkew Area. When he returned he told me that he
had been abducted this morning on Woosung Road near Range
Road by a party of Japanese and Chinese, about 7 or 8 in
number, all in civilian clothes, who bound him with rope.
His Japanese employer on seeing him being taken away made a
request to the party which resulted in his being released.
At 3 p.m. 5-3-40, I met Oong Ching Sung outside my house.
He asked me if I knew anyone who had recently been abducted
by Japanese. I then told him what my tenant had related to
me. At his request, I took Oong Ching Sung to Ying Ching
Woo's room where I found him sitting on his bed. Oong Ching
Sung asked his name and later attempted to take him to the
Japanese Garrison Headquarters. However he refused, and
Oong Ching Sung then took possession of his blue 'pass' and
left, returning together with a Japanese soldier afterwards
when they forcibly took Ying Ching Woo away. I do not know
anything further.

This is my true statement.

So: Tsah Dah Sung.

1940年3月4日上午10时许，一名泥瓦匠应庆武（Ying Ching Woo，音译）搬入吾宅。1940年3月5日上午，他前往虹口区做工。返回时，他告知我，今晨在吴淞路近兰路（Range Road）处，被一伙约七八人的日本人和中国人绑架，这些人均着便衣，并用绳索捆绑了他。他的日本雇主目睹其被带走，向该伙人提出交涉，致使他获释。1940年3月5日下午3时，我在屋外遇见翁庆松（Oong Ching Sung，音译）。他问我是否认识近期被日本人绑架的人。我便将租户告诉我的情况转述给他。应其要求，我带翁庆松到应庆武的房间，见他正坐在床上。翁庆松询问其姓名，随后试图将他带往日本兵营司令部。然而应庆武拒绝，翁庆松遂拿走其蓝色“通行证”后离开，之后与一名日本士兵一同返回，强行将应庆武带走。此后情况我一概不知。

以上为本人真实陈述。

签署：蔡达松（Tsah Dah Sung）。

It will be noted that the victim's wrists had
not been bound by a rope as mentioned in my previous
report. This exposes the fact that such incidents when
passed along usually become exaggerated. As regards his
private assistant he was not sure if he had been taken
away and also his cousin did not travel on the particular
bus mentioned which is also another exposition of the
magnification of the incident.

Inquiries were made by the undersigned at the
scene where the hold up was made and it was discovered
that Kinchow Road, where the affair occurred, was not
made up and there were factory walls on either side,
but no inhabitants nearby, consequently an ideal place
to carry out such an action mentioned.

Tseu Bing Rong, age 30, single, residing 57 Noa Dah
Lee (立德里) in Central Style, French Concession, employed
in the Investigation Department of the Yue Tsong Tobacco Co.

At about 10 a.m. 7/3/40, I was instructed by my
department chief Mr. Ho to make inquiries at Kung Yung (公永)
Tobacco Factory at Lane 496, House No. 3 and Road in
connection with the "Nelson" cigarette. I boarded a route
No. 7 Japanese bus on Avenue Joffre near Szechow Road and
proceeded to my destination. About 20 minutes later, the
bus arrived at the corner of Foki and Kinchow Roads where I
intended to alight from the bus. As I was getting down from
the bus, saw seven persons in civilian clothes. Two among
them in Chinese clothes approached me, seized hold of
both my arms. I asked them the reason for their doing so.
One of them stated "Military Headquarters" and took me along
Kinchow Road North of Foki Road. At that time, I told them
that I was a proper business man so they searched me. One
of them said to me in Chinese with a Japanese accent "Have
you any money?" I answered in the affirmative and handed to
him twenty dollars in notes which was all the money I had.
This man at once told me to go. So I boarded a Japanese No. 7
bus and returned to the company.

At the time I was taken to Kinchow Road I saw four
Chinese standing on the same road and were being searched by
the abovementioned seven persons. These four Chinese also

以下为周秉荣（Tseu Bing Rong）之陈述，系宁波籍人，由本人 D.J. Cheng Yuan Ching 于 1940 年 3 月 7 日录取，并由 D.J. Cheng Yuan Ching 翻译。

周秉荣，30 岁，未婚，住法租界中央里（Central Style）立德里 57 号，受雇于岳中烟草公司调查部。

1940 年 3 月 7 日上午 10 时许，我奉本部门主管何先生之命，前往位于 496 弄 3 号的公永（Kung Yung）烟草厂，就“纳尔逊”（Nelson）牌香烟一事进行查问。我在霞飞路近四川路处搭乘了一辆日本 7 路公共汽车，前往目的地。约 20 分钟后，汽车抵达福建路与锦州路转角处，我正准备下车。当我下车时，看见七名便衣人员。其中两名身穿中式服装的人走近我，抓住我的双臂。我问他们为何如此行事。其中一人称“军事司令部”，并挟持我沿福建路以北的锦州路前行。当时，我告诉他们我是正当商人，于是他们对我进行了搜身。其中一人用带有日本口音的中文问我：“你有钱吗？”我予以肯定回答，并将身上仅有的二十元纸币交给了他。此人随即让我离开。于是我搭乘日本 7 路公共汽车返回公司。

在我被带往锦州路时，我看见四名中国人站在同一条路上，正被上述七人搜身。这四名中国人也是从同一辆公共汽车上下来的，并被那七人沿锦州路带走。

Sir,

With reference to Lee Yue Liang (李有良),
houseboy, employed by Mr. S.C. Pemberton, attached to
Hongkew Fire Brigade Station, he was called to Hongkew
Police Station on the evening of March 6th, 1940 to
give a statement disclosing what knowledge he had of
Press Gangs functioning North of the Creek in the
International Settlement. The statement, attached,
herewith, was duly taken on his arrival and a summary
of it is as follows:-

"Owing to the wide rumour in circulation
in Hongkew District to the effect that
Chinese were being kidnapped by Japanese
I was afraid to go out. However, in
the event of it being necessary to go outside,
and to protect myself, I asked my employer
to give me a Fire Brigade uniform to show I
was in foreign employ."

Lee Yue Liang is now wearing a Fire Brigade
cap and blue coat. Mr. S.C. Pemberton when interviewed
stated it was never alleged that his houseboy had been
taken away by a Press Gang but he only remarked about
the servant's fear.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

Alexander Telfer

先生：

关于受雇于隶属虹口救火会站的 S.C. Pemberton 先生的男仆李有良（Lee Yue Liang），他于 1940 年 3 月 6 日晚被召至虹口巡捕房，就其所知关于在国际租界苏州河以北地区活动的抓壮丁团伙的情况提供陈述。随函附上在其到达时按规定录取的陈述书，其摘要如下：-

“由于虹口区广泛流传着中国人正被日本人绑架的谣言，我不敢外出。然而，若确有必要外出，为保护自身安全，我请求雇主给我一套救火会制服，以表明我是受外籍人士雇佣。”

李有良目前戴着一顶救火会帽子，身穿蓝色外套。S.C. Pemberton 先生在接受问询时表示，从未有人指控其男仆被拉夫队抓走，他只是提到了该仆人的恐惧心理。

1940年3月6日下午5时30分，我从虹口救火会站来到巡捕房报案，称我已受雇于一位名为彭伯顿（Pemberton）的外国人担任男仆，历时四年。
由于担心被日本人绑架，且此类谣言在虹口区广泛流传，我不敢外出；为求自保，我在必须外出时，曾请求雇主给我一套救火会制服，以表明我受雇于外人。
鉴于若有中国人被日本人绑架，其生命将被视如蝼蚁，为此我请求上海公共租界警务处尽力保护我们的安全，以维护我们的权益。

李月良签字并画押。

Sir,

Vide reports published in the local press of alleged "press gangs" operating in areas north of the creek, Mr. Sampson of the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury telephoned this station on the morning of the 5/3/40 stating that one of their delivery coolie had made the following report when reporting for duty at 9 a.m. 5/3/40.

At about 6.30 p.m. 4/3/40 he had been stopped at Glen and Pingliang Road corner by Japanese plain clothes men and ordered into a yellow truck containing 7 other Chinese but had escaped and run to Yangtszepoo Station where he had stayed the night with an Indian.

Mr. Sampson was asked to send the coolie to this station with a view to checking his story, since a careful examination of all books and duties failed to reveal any indication that the coolie had come to the station.

At 6.45 p.m. 6/3/40 the coolie, Tsang Yoong Ching (  ) arrived at the station and was questioned by C.D.S. 108 and D.S. Barker-Smith. On Poyang Road near Kweiyang Road, he states, a M/truck in which were a number of male Chinese coming from the East stopped, and from this, three male Japanese in plain clothes alighted and stopped him. 先生：

鉴于本地报刊刊登了关于苏州河以北地区据称有“抓壮丁团伙”活动的报道，《上海晚邮与信使报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）的桑普森（Sampson）先生于1940年3月5日上午致电本巡捕房，称其一名送报苦力在当日上午9时报到时作了如下陈述。

据称，在1940年3月4日下午6时30分左右，他在格兰路（Glen Road）与平凉路路口被便衣日本男子拦下，并被命令进入一辆载有其他7名中国人的黄色卡车，但他随后逃脱并跑至杨树浦巡捕房，当晚与一名印度人一同留宿于此。

鉴于对所有登记簿和执勤记录的仔细核查均未发现该苦力曾来到巡捕房的任何迹象，我们要求桑普森先生将该苦力送至本巡捕房，以便核实其说法。

1940年3月6日下午6时45分，该苦力曾永清（Tsang Yoong Ching，音译）抵达巡捕房，并接受刑事侦缉警佐（C.D.S.）108号及警佐（D.S.）巴克-史密斯的讯问。他随后陈述称，1940年3月5日下午7时30分左右，他在波阳路（Poyang Road）的培顿鲍尔温纱厂（Paton & Baldwins Mill）送完报纸后，骑自行车向西离去。他称，在波阳路靠近贵阳路（Kweiyang Road）处，一辆从东面驶来、载有多名中国男子的摩托卡车停下，车上下来三名便衣日本男子并将其拦下。这些人询问他的职业，随后对他进行了搜身。此时，三名中国男子走近，日本人离开了

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tsan : Yoon : Ching ( 叶永 ),
native of Hunan taken by me C. L. S. 108
at Y'poo Stn. on the 5/3/40 and translated
and interpreted by Clerk C. J. Chin.

My name is Tsan, Yoong Ching ( ), age 37, native
of Hunan, M/newspaper-sender, residing in Chekiang Road Refugee
Camp, Chekiang Road.

At about 7 p.m. on the 4/3/40 I delivered a copy of Evening
Post Newspaper to the Patons & Baldwins Woollen Factory
situated on Poyang Road and after delivering the paper I left
the woollen factory by riding a bicycle and on Poyang Road near
Kweiyang Road I observed a m/truck in opposite direction from
which three Japanese civilians dropped and stopped me. They
asked me what my occupation was, I replied that I was a
newspaper-sender in the employ of the Evening Post Press, and
they then searched me. At this juncture they observed three
male Chinese walking on Poyang Road from East to West, and after
they had told me to wait a while, the three Japanese civilians
approached the three male Chinese. I took this opportunity and
left this place by riding my bicycle. Being afraid that I would
be chased by the Japanese civilians I stopped on the corner of
Pingliang and Glen Roads and placed the bicycle in the field
nearby. I waited on this corner until 5 a.m. 5/3/40 and then
I rode my bicycle to a wine shop on Yangchow Road where I had
some wine, and at about 7.30 a.m. 5/3/40 I left the wine shop
and proceeded to the Evening Post Office, arriving there at
about 8.15 a.m. 5/3/40. At the office I told the above story
but I did not say that I was stopped by an Indian Policeman and
I did not say that I reported the matter at the Police Station.

9.1.

Signed: Tsang Yoong Ching.

以下为叶永（Tsan : Yoon : Ching）之供词，该员系湖南人，由本人 C. L. S. 108 于 1940 年 3 月 5 日在杨树浦巡捕房录取，并由书记员 C. J. Chin 翻译及传译。

本人姓名叶永（Tsan, Yoong Ching），现年 37 岁，湖南人，职业为送报员，现住浙江路难民收容所，位于浙江路。

1940 年 3 月 4 日晚 7 时许，我将一份《晚报》送至位于鄱阳路的 Patons & Baldwins 毛纺厂，送报后我骑自行车离开该毛纺厂，在鄱阳路近贵阳路处，我看见对面驶来一辆机动卡车，车上下来三名日本平民并拦住了我。他们询问我的职业，我回答我是《晚报》馆雇用的送报员，随后他们对我进行了搜身。此时，他们看见三名中国男子沿鄱阳路由东向西行走，在让我稍候片刻后，这三名日本平民走向那三名中国男子。我趁此机会骑自行车离开了该地。因担心被日本平民追赶，我在平凉路与格兰路（Glen Road）（音译）的拐角处停下，将自行车藏在附近的田野中。我在该拐角处一直等到 1940 年 3 月 5 日凌晨 5 时，然后骑车前往扬州路的一家酒铺喝了些酒，并于 1940 年 3 月 5 日上午 7 时 30 分左右离开酒铺，前往《晚报》馆，于 1940 年 3 月 5 日上午 8 时 15 分左右抵达。在报馆我讲述了上述经过，但我未提及曾被一名印度巡捕拦下，也未提及我曾向巡捕房报告此事。

9.1.

Special Patrol

Between 4.15 a.m. and 7.30 a.m. 7-3-40 D.S.I.
Beloshenko and the undersigned patrolled the entire Hongkew
District in separate units. Particular attention was
paid to Bridges, street intersections, bus-stops and
places where workers congregate. Parts of Kashing Road
and Wayside districts were also visited.

Even before dawn large numbers of vegetable hawkers
and early workers were to be seen on the streets which
appeared even more busy than those of the areas South of

No untoward incident occurred and nothing of a
suspicious nature was seen.

offered him $3.00. Brought to the Station and questioned

page_data.en:
North Area
Kidnapping
Denied

Japanese Ask for Proof
Of Newspaper Reports

Reports of alleged kidnappings carried out by the Japanese authorities north of the creek, that have appeared in the local press recently, were vehemently denied by Japanese spokesmen at the Japanese press conference yesterday. "From the character of the reports," the Embassy spokesman stated, "they appear to be a piece of propaganda being circulated by certain elements with a definite purpose in view."

As far as the Japanese authorities were concerned no such activities were taking place in the Japanese controlled areas of Shanghai, he continued. A Navy spokesman added that the Japanese Naval Landing Party had investigated those allegations and had discovered no facts tending to confirm, in any way, statements made by one newspaper.

Evidence Wanted

He then asked if the allegations published in the press implicated the Japanese Naval Landing Party. He was told by one journalist present that the name of the Landing Party had not been mentioned in any of the reports. "Have you any evidence to support these allegations?" the spokesman asked.

He continued, "As stated before there might have been arrests of Chinese suspects by the Japanese Naval Landing Party such as suspicious individuals or criminals. There has been no detention of men for use in forced labour by the Japanese authorities or at the latter's instigation."

The Navy spokesman added that he felt it was extremely regrettable that such rumours tending to make Chinese afraid to venture north of the creek were being circulated. If any concrete information about the alleged kidnappings was available, he said, the Japanese Naval Landing Party would be grateful to receive it. Names of victims, places, times, circumstances and the source of information were required.

Japanese Newspaper Comment

Action would be taken by Japanese consular police, Japanese Settlement Defence Corps, Japanese Gendarmerie and the Municipality of Shanghai to stop false reports that Chinese were being kidnapped in Hongkew and sent to Formosa, the "Tairiku Shimpo" reported yesterday.

The false reports originated with the publication in a Chinese language paper in the Settlement that Mr. Li Chin-ken, 33, shop assistant of the Taishodo, 314 Woosung Road, was kidnapped by a gang, the paper said. Showing that the reports were false, Mr. Li was still working in the Japanese store, the "Tairiku" stated.

The "Tairiku" charged that there was a connection between the false reports and the activities of the underlings of Mr. Wu Kai-hsien, leader of an anti-Japanese group under the control of Chungking.
page_data.zh:
北区
绑架
否认

日方要求提供
报纸报道的证据

日本发言人在昨日的日本记者招待会上，强烈否认了近期本地报刊上出现的、关于日本当局在苏州河以北地区实施所谓绑架行为的报道。使馆发言人称：“从这些报道的性质来看，它们似乎是某些带有明确目的的元素所散布的宣传品。”

他继续表示，就日本当局而言，在上海的日本控制区内并未发生此类活动。一位海军发言人补充说，日本海军陆战队已对这些指控进行了调查，未发现任何事实能在任何方面证实某家报纸所作的陈述。

要求提供证据

随后，他询问报刊上发表的指控是否牵涉到日本海军陆战队。在场的一位记者告诉他，任何报道中均未提及海军陆战队的名称。“你们有任何证据支持这些指控吗？”该发言人问道。

他接着说：“如前所述，日本海军陆战队可能逮捕了一些中国嫌疑人，例如可疑分子或罪犯。但日本当局或其唆使下，并未拘禁人员用于强迫劳动。”

这位海军发言人补充说，他感到极为遗憾的是，正在流传此类使中国人不敢冒险前往苏州河以北的谣言。他说，如果有关于所谓绑架的任何具体信息，日本海军陆战队将不胜感激。需要提供受害者姓名、地点、时间、情况以及信息来源。

日本报纸评论

据《大陆新报》昨日报道，日本领事警察、日本居留民团防卫队、日本宪兵队以及上海市政府将采取行动，制止关于中国人正在虹口被绑架并送往台湾的虚假报道。

该报称，这些虚假报道源于租界内一份中文报纸刊登的消息，称吴淞路314号泰昌号（Taishodo）33岁的店员李金根（Li Chin-ken，音译）先生被一伙歹徒绑架。《大陆新报》指出，李先生的确仍在该日本商店工作，以此证明报道失实。

《大陆新报》指责这些虚假报道与受重庆控制的反日团体首领吴凯先（Wu Kai-hsien，音译）先生手下的活动有关联。

No Illegal
Activities
Conducted

Rumours In Press Are
Strongly Denied By
Naval Spokesman

Again repeating that no such
"slave traffic" or "press gangs" was
taking place in the Japanese con-
trolled areas, the navy spokesman
at the press conference last even-

have appeared in the columns of

The Japanese Naval Landing

There have been no facts tending

The spokesman made reference to

store, the "Tairiku" stated.

The "Tairiku" charged that there
was a connection between the false
reports and the activities of the

under the control of Chungking.
page_data.zh:
未进行
非法活动

海军发言人
强烈否认报界谣言

在昨晚的新闻发布会上，海军发言人再次重申，在日本控制的区域内并未发生此类“奴隶贸易”或“抓壮丁”行为，并坚决否认中文及部分外文报刊专栏中出现的所谓日军在苏州河以北地区从事此类强制活动的“谣言、指控和报道”。

该发言人表示，日本海军陆战队对有关其“绑架”中国人从事劳工项目的报道被不公正地流传深感遗憾。

发言人称，没有任何事实倾向于证实这些报道。其中大多数报道的性质似乎纯粹是某些人出于特定原因散布的宣传。

发言人提及昨晨《字林西报》（North China Daily News）专栏中刊登的一篇此类报道，该报道称有证据表明此类行径正在发生；发言人指出，这根本没有任何证据或事实依据。

无非法逮捕

《字林西报》记者告知发言人，其数据系从警务处副总监处获得。

发言人回答说，日本陆战队未曾进行任何非法逮捕。他 stated，当然曾逮捕过可疑人员或罪犯，但正如指控所言，这些被捕或被拘留者均未被日本人强迫加入任何劳工队。

发言人说：“我重申，这些谣言的流传令人极为遗憾，它们导致中国人在控制区内感到不安全。”

领事行动

据《大陆新报》（Tairiku Shimpo）昨日报道，日本领事警察、日本居留民团防卫队、日本宪兵队以及上海市政府将采取行动，制止关于中国人虹口被绑架并送往台湾的虚假报道。

该报称，虚假报道源于租界内一份中文报纸刊登的消息，称吴淞路314号泰昌号（Taishodo）33岁的店员李金根（Li Chin-ken，音译）先生被一伙人绑架。《大陆新报》指出，李先生仍在该日商店铺工作，以此证明报道失实。

《大陆新报》指控称，这些虚假报道与重庆方面控制的反日团体首领吴凯先（Wu Kai-hsien，音译）先生手下人的活动有关联。

page_data.en:
North of Creek
"Press Gangs"
Investigated

Evidence of Practice
And Camp in Pootung
Brought to Light

Although repeated denials of the practice had been made by the Japanese spokesmen here, the "North-China Daily News" yesterday received definite confirmation of the widespread reports that the Japanese are forcibly removing young Chinese men from the area north of the Soochow Creek—recently reopened to the Chinese generally—and using them on work projects in Pootung and elsewhere. A number of concrete cases of such abductions, in Chapei, Hongkew, Wayside and Yangtszepoo, have come to light, indicating an organized "slave traffic" which fully justifies the apprehension now felt by the Chinese population generally, a feeling which has already been reflected in the columns of the Chinese press.

In many instances the Chinese victims of this racket have simply vanished leaving no trace. In some cases they have been lucky enough to elude the "press gang" operating on the streets at dusk or at night, at the same time seeing their less fortunate brethren in the clutches of the kidnappers. In one instance a coolie was taken to a labour concentration camp in Pootung, where he was lodged with about 100 others under a guard of armed Japanese and Chinese. He managed to escape and tell his story. Already the spiriting away of all these young Chinese, some of them married and the heads of families, has had a marked discouraging effect on the return of the Chinese population to the northern areas and has created a state there approaching panic.

Scare Created Among Chinese

In this connection it is learned that mill workers, delivery coolies and others having business over the bridges are reluctant to go into the area, while the male servants of families residing "north of the Creek" are fearful of appearing on the streets, especially after dark. Kidnappings have been reported close to the bridges over the Soochow Creek as well as at various points in the district generally, near the Hongkew Market, the North Railway Station, in the vicinity of the large mills, and so forth. No part of the reopened area seems safe.

Various cases can be quoted in evidence of the virtual slave traffic. At 5.30 a.m. on Monday, some forty minutes before sunrise, a Chinese witness was walking along Boone Road near the intersection of North Szechuen Road when he saw three men stop some Chinese labourers and force three of them to accompany them. One of the victims made a struggle but apparently did not succeed in escaping. The witness was unable to ascertain whether the abductors were Chinese, Korean or Japanese.

Shot by Soldiers

The day previous a Chinese was walking in Chapei, west of the North Railway Station, when, according to his story, four Japanese soldiers seized him for the purpose of forcing him into a labour corps. He made a break away from them, and he was immediately fired upon and slightly wounded. He had run far enough, however, to regain his freedom and he made his way back to the Settlement south of the Soochow Creek. The next morning he sought medical aid and he is now in a local hospital under treatment for two bullet wounds in his legs. A full report of his experience has been made to the proper authorities. Foreign observers have previously noted the presence of young Chinese with their hands tied behind their backs in the neighbourhood of the North Station, in Chapei.

A few days before the shooting near the North Station, a young Chinese was walking in the vicinity of Yangtszepoo Road and Thorburn Road when he was accosted by two men in foreign clothes who spoke a language which he recognized as Japanese. He was ordered to stop and to go with the men to a canvas-covered motor-lorry parked at the kerb near by. He noticed that at the moment another Chinese was being forced into the vehicle. At this juncture a public omnibus made a halt at the corner and the intended victim of the press gang managed to board it. Once on the bus, he said, he looked back at the standing lorry and saw between twenty and thirty Chinese inside it. He thanked his lucky star for a narrow escape.

Taken to Pootung Camp

The most illuminating case, however, concerns a young married Chinese, a resident of the Wayside district and a mill worker by trade. This man was halted on Liaoyang Road at 5 a.m. on February 15 by a Japanese soldier who made him accompany him to a Japanese military post near by. As he showed signs of resistance he was threatened with shooting. Half an hour later he was bundled into a covered truck with about forty other able-bodied Chinese and driven to one of the eastern wharves. They were placed in a large boat which was towed by a launch to the Pootung side. There they disembarked and were marched for a couple of hours until they reached a camp, surrounded by barbed wire and guarded by a small force of Japanese soldiers and a larger force of Chinese police. He estimated that there were fifty conscripts in the camp before the arrival of the fresh lot.

The following morning all the prisoners were taken out to perform highway construction work, still under guard. In the evening they were returned to the camp. They were given reasonably good food but were not paid a cent for their hard work. After a week the new prisoner and some of his fellows succeeded in escaping at night and they made a long trek finally reaching the bank of the Whangpoo. The young man who had been kidnapped in Liaoyang Road managed to return to the Shanghai side of the river last week, much weakened by his precarious journey. He is now under treatment at a local hospital—south of the Soochow Creek.

Reported Shipped to Nanking

Another case deals with a young Chinese who is reported to have been abducted near the north end of the Garden Bridge two weeks ago and sent to Nanking to work as a coolie. This man has managed to inform his relatives of his whereabouts by letter. He is believed to be still in Nanking.

In yet another instance a Chinese was forcibly removed from the street in Hongkew near the Chapoo Road Bridge on February 25. No trace has been found of this man.
page_data.zh:
苏州河以北
“抓壮丁”行为
受调查

实践证据
及浦东营地
被揭露

尽管驻沪日本发言人一再否认此类行为，但《字林西报》昨日收到确切证实，印证了广泛流传的报告：日本人正从苏州河以北地区（最近已重新向一般华人开放）强行带走年轻中国男子，并将他们用于浦东及其他地方的工程项目。在闸北、虹口、魏司德（Wayside，音译）和杨树浦，已发现多起此类绑架的具体案例，表明存在一种有组织的“奴隶贸易”，这完全证明了目前中国民众普遍感到的担忧是合理的，这种情绪也已反映在中国报刊的版面上。

在许多情况下，这一勒索勾当的中国受害者 simply 消失得无影无踪。在某些情况下，受害者足够幸运，得以避开黄昏或夜间在街道上活动的“抓壮丁”团伙，同时目睹了他们不那么幸运的同胞落入绑匪之手。在一个案例中，一名苦力被带往浦东的一个劳工集中营，在那里他与大约100其他人一起被关押，由武装的日本人和中国人看守。他设法逃脱并讲述了自己的经历。所有这些年轻中国人的被秘密带走，其中一些人已婚且为家庭支柱，已经对华人人口返回北部地区产生了显著的阻碍作用，并在当地造成了一种近乎恐慌的状态。

在华人群中引发恐慌

就此而言，据悉，工厂工人、送货苦力以及其他需要过桥办事的人都不愿进入该区域，而居住在“苏州河以北”的家庭的男仆则害怕出现在街道上，尤其是在天黑之后。据报道，绑架事件发生在苏州河桥梁附近，以及该地区的各个地点，如虹口市场、北站、大型工厂附近等。重新开放的区域似乎没有一处是安全的。

可以列举各种案例作为这种实质上的奴隶贸易的证据。周一凌晨5点30分，即日出前约四十分钟，一名中国证人在四川北路与百老汇路（Boone Road）交叉口附近行走时，看到三名男子拦住了一些中国劳工，并强迫其中三人随他们离开。其中一名受害者进行了挣扎，但显然未能成功逃脱。证人无法确定绑架者是中国人、朝鲜人还是日本人。

被士兵开枪射击

前一天，一名中国人在闸北、北站以西行走时，据其陈述，四名日本士兵抓住他，目的是强迫他加入劳工队。他挣脱逃跑，随即遭到枪击并受轻伤。然而，他已跑出了足够远的距离以重获自由，并回到了苏州河以南的租界。第二天早上他寻求医疗救助，目前他在当地一家医院接受治疗，腿部有两处枪伤。他的全部经历已向有关当局作了完整报告。外国观察家此前曾注意到，在闸北北站附近，有双手被反绑在背后的年轻中国人。

在北站附近发生枪击事件前几天，一名年轻中国人在杨树浦路与索伯恩路（Thorburn Road，音译）附近行走时，被两名身穿西式服装的男子搭讪，这两人说着他能辨认出是日语的语言。他被命令停下，并随这些人前往停在附近路边的一辆盖着帆布的机动卡车。他注意到当时另一名中国人正被强行塞进车内。就在此时，一辆公共汽车在拐角处停下，这名抓壮丁团伙的预定受害者设法登上了公交车。他说，一旦上了车，他回头看向那辆停着的卡车，看到里面有二三十名中国人。他庆幸自己死里逃生。

被带往浦东营地

然而，最具启发性的案例涉及一名年轻的已婚中国人，他是魏司德（Wayside，音译）区的居民，职业为工厂工人。2月15日凌晨5点，此人在辽阳路被一名日本士兵拦下，被迫随其前往附近的日本军事哨所。由于他表现出抵抗迹象，受到开枪威胁。半小时后，他与大约四十名其他身强力壮的中国人一起被塞进一辆有篷卡车，被驱往东部的一个码头。他们被置于一艘大船上，由一艘汽艇拖曳至浦东一侧。在那里他们上岸，并被列队行进了几个小时，直到到达一个营地，该营地周围环绕着铁丝网，由一小队日本士兵和一大队中国警察看守。他估计，在这批新人到达之前，营地里已有五十名被征召者。

第二天早上，所有囚犯仍在看守下被带出去进行公路建设工作。晚上他们被带回营地。他们得到的食物相当不错，但其辛勤工作未获得分文报酬。一周后，这名新囚犯和一些同伴在夜间成功逃脱，经过长途跋涉，最终到达黄浦江岸。这名在辽阳路被绑架的年轻人上周设法回到了上海的江边，因这段危险的旅程而身体极度虚弱。他目前正在苏州河以南的一家当地医院接受治疗。

据报被运往南京

另一起案例涉及一名年轻中国人，据报两周前在花园桥北端附近被绑架，并被送往南京做苦力。此人已通过信件设法告知亲属其下落。据信他仍在南京。

还有一例，2月25日，一名中国人在虹口靠近乍浦路桥的街道上被强行带走。至今未发现此人的踪迹。
